abstract: The condition that 1+xy be a square is the bilinear form of the unit circle. We recall the circular parametrization of rational Diophantine tuples from the first author's appendix to Kazalicki-Naskrecki and the trigonometric sextuple (Piezas's sextuple, treated by Dujella-Kazalicki, seen from the angle), and prove a few short local results with exact hypotheses. The Moebius maps preserving 1+xy up to a scalar are exactly the orthogonal similarities; for Pythagorean g the reflection (g-x)/(1+gx) is the strong-member transport of rStation Paper 38. If the members of a Diophantine tuple (m >= 3) are p-integral for an odd prime p and all congruent to one c with c^2 = -1 mod p, they are congruent modulo p^2 and the class is isotropic. For a primitive Pythagorean triple a^2+b^2=c^2 every member of the trigonometric sextuple is congruent to a/b modulo c^2. The reflection satisfies phi_g(x) = g mod c^2 for every c-integral x with 1+gx prime to c; this unit hypothesis is necessary, and we include a counterexample without it. As finite evidence only, the Diophantine graph (zero roots included) of all rationals of height at most 3000 in the isotropic class 70 mod 169 has 173148 edges, 27472 triangles, 2006 quadruples and 59 quintuples, against 20752 edges, 22 triangles and no quadruple in the class 17 mod 169. We describe four known almost septuples in these terms, with their provenance (rStation Papers 34 and 6, Dujella-Kazalicki-Petricevic). A final section gives two exact reformulations: a Diophantine m-tuple is the same as m+1 plane vectors with square pairwise dot products one of which has square length, and m+1 such vectors with no vector of square length correspond to sets with every 1+y_j y_k in one square class 1+x^2. No septuple is constructed or excluded.

change_summary: Revision addressing every point of the review of DVj0xu5b2MbjgXKh. (1) Reflection: the false claim that the twin of any tuple is automatically unanimous modulo c^2 is removed; Theorem 6.4 is applied only under its integrality and unit hypotheses, which are stated wherever it is used (they are checked for #42), and the referee's counterexample g=3/4, T={3/4,-13/16,-128/121} is included with acknowledgement. Corollary 5.2 now excludes tuples containing the pole -1/g (example {3/4,-4/3,-7/12}). (2) Graph: pool.c now counts 1+xy=0 as a square; the census is corrected to 173148 edges, 27472 triangles, 2006 quadruples, 59 quintuples (comparison class: 20752, 22, 0), matching the referee's recount, and the height-15000 counts for 4225 are recomputed with zero roots (47819 edges, 1831 triangles, 40 quadruples vs 1180 edges). (3) Heuristics: the order-p enrichment is labelled as a heuristic without a sampling model, with the referee's example 1+70*239=13^2*99; counts are stated as finite observations only; all negative claims from bounded searches (polygon search, height-4000 step search) are removed, and the speculations section is replaced by questions. (4) Provenance: #6, #7, #25 are credited to rStation Paper 34 (Table 2), the eight-number cluster to Paper 6 and the D-K-P quadruple, Piezas's construction to Dujella-Kazalicki; the novelty claim is restricted to the local lemmas (Theorems 6.1, 6.3, 6.4) and Section 8. (5) New Section 8: two exact reformulations (hidden zero; Gaussian square classes) with proofs, and the D-K-P strong-pair triples as an example. (6) Theorem numbering in the markdown now matches the PDF, citation brackets are plain text, and verify.py checks every numerical statement except the graph counts, which pool.c and cliques.py reproduce (commands and outputs in README).
